summary: Edith Wyschogrod was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. She earned her B.A. from Hunter College and her Ph.D. from Columbia University before serving as J. Newton Rayzor Professor of Philosophy and Religious Thought at Rice University from 1992 to 2002.
Edmond Yee is a religious studies scholar and sinologist. Around 1985, he held faculty posts at both the Pacific Lutheran Theological Seminary and the Graduate Theological Union.

Edmund Hardy worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Mainz, Heidelberg under Kuno Fischer, Freiburg, and Berlin. He was a philosophy professor at Freiburg (1885-1893) and held a chair in comparative religion and ancient Indian literature at Fribourg (1894-1898).

Edmund Leach was an anthropologist and religious studies scholar educated at Clare College, Cambridge, and the London School of Economics. He lectured at the LSE (1947-1953) and served as professor at Cambridge (1953-1978), provost of King's College (1966-1979), and president of the RAI (1971-1975).
Edmund Nathaniel Snyder was an Indologist who graduated as valedictorian from Harvard University in 1886. He also studied under Albrecht Weber and Hermann Oldenberg.

Edo Shonin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and psychology. In 2015, he was attested as a research psychologist at Nottingham Trent University and Research Director at the Awake to Wisdom Centre for Meditation and Mindfulness Research.

Eduard Böhmer was a linguist who studied at the Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg from around 1847 to 1851. He held academic posts at Halle-Wittenberg (1859-1872) and the University of Strasbourg (circa 1872-1879).

Eduard Erkes was a sinologist who studied under August Conrady at Leipzig University. He spent his career holding academic posts at Leipzig University (circa 1917-1958) and Humboldt University of Berlin (circa 1947-1958).

Eduard Hermann was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Freiburg, Leipzig, and Jena under Berthold Delbrück. He held posts at Kiel (1913) and Frankfurt (1914) before serving as professor at the University of Göttingen from 1917 to 1937.

Eduard Müller was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He completed his inaugural dissertation at Leipzig University around 1872-1874 and served as a professor at the University of Bern from circa 1886 to 1908.

Eduard Röer, a scholar of Indology and philosophy, studied at Königsberg and Jena under Johann Friedrich Herbart, and later under Franz Bopp. He held posts at Humboldt University, the East India Company, and The Asiatic Society.

Eduard Sachau was an Orientalist, linguist, and historian who studied at Kiel, Leipzig, and Halle under Theodor Nöldeke, Hermann Brockhaus, and Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer. He was an associate professor at Vienna and held chairs at Frederick William University Berlin and the Seminar for Oriental Languages.

Eduard Schwyzer was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. Over his academic career, he held posts at the University of Zurich (circa 1912-1927), the University of Bonn (circa 1927-1932), and Humboldt University of Berlin (circa 1932-1943).

Eduard Sievers was a linguist educated at Leipzig and Berlin under Georg Curtius, August Leskien, and Friedrich Zarncke. He served as professor at the universities of Jena (1871-1883), Tübingen (1883-1887), Halle-Wittenberg (1887-1892), and Leipzig (1892-1922).

Eduardo Francisco Freyre Roach is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his Master of Buddhist Studies at The University of Hong Kong under the supervision of Y. Karunadasa and Georgios T. Halkias, attested in 2014.

Edvard Westermarck was a philosopher and scholar of religious studies who studied at the University of Helsinki. He later held academic positions at the London School of Economics (circa 1904-1930) and Åbo Akademi University (circa 1918-1932).

Edward Albert Gait was a historian and Indologist who studied at University College London from around 1880 to 1882. He founded the Bihar and Orissa Research Society in 1914 and served as its president from 1915 to 1920.

Edward Backhouse Eastwick worked in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Charterhouse, Oxford, and Merton College, he served as Professor of Hindustani and Telugu at East India Company College (1845) and worked for the Foreign Office (circa 1860-1863).

Edward Byles Cowell studied at Oxford under Horace Hayman Wilson, working in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian studies. He was principal at Sanskrit College (1858-1864) and professor of history at Presidency University (1856) before becoming professor at Cambridge (1867-1903).

Edward C. Dimock Jr. was a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and linguistics who studied at Yale and Harvard (Ph.D. 1959). He served as an assistant professor at the University of Chicago (1966-1993) and president of the AIIS (1972-1986).
